name: Skull-lens ultrasound brain scanner
subtitle: a headset that maps brain activity through bone

effects.effect: tiny repeated structures bend light, sound or radio the 'wrong' way

effect: tiny repeated structures bend light, sound or radio the 'wrong' way
how: Brain scanners that track thought, like fMRI, fill a room, and functional ultrasound, which watches blood rush to busy brain areas, works only through a hole in the skull. A thin cap patterned with tiny structures, shaped from a scan of the wearer's own skull, pre-bends the sound to cancel the bone's distortion, so a headset could map brain activity through intact bone.
obstacle: Bone soaks up most of the high-pitched sound needed for sharp images, leaving very faint echoes.
why: Functional ultrasound needs a skull window today; skull-correcting lenses are only bench tests.
real: 3D-printed binary acoustic metasurfaces corrected skull aberration to focus ultrasound through ex vivo human skulls (Frontiers in Neuroscience 2022), but none has been used for transcranial functional ultrasound imaging.
